# SB-1048 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated by dry media blasting operations can present inhalation hazards, combustible dust risks in confined zones, and surface contamination that impacts downstream heat treat performance. Recent observations on P2, line P2-L4 blasting stations show fugitive dust migrating into adjacent work zones and into the heat treat room serving EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Airborne particulates from blasting can adhere to workpieces and furnace internals, increasing the potential for furnace contamination and creating maintenance burdens. In addition, increased particulate loading on filters and ventilation elements raises the risk of unexpected service interruptions and degraded air quality for personnel.

Background: Blasting is a necessary pre-heat-treat cleaning step on P2, line P2-L4 to remove scale and prepare surfaces for treatment in EQ-P2-L4-HT02. However, when blasting containment and local extraction controls fail or are insufficient, dust can escape the blast booth envelope and accumulate where it creates safety and process-control issues. This bulletin addresses controls to limit airborne dust exposure and to prevent migration into EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

Rationale: Controlling dust at source reduces inhalation exposure, minimizes combustible dust layering, and preserves heat treat furnace integrity. Mitigation measures also lower long-term maintenance and downtime by preventing abrasive or reactive dust from entering furnace load paths.

Applicable documents: ECN-2026-020, MM-P2-L4-HT02, SOP-P2-L4-03

## Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P2-L4-HT02 (Heat Treat furnace number two serving line P2-L4)  
Stations: All blasting booths and work cells on P2, line P2-L4 that perform dry media blasting prior to furnace loading.  
Supporting: Local ventilation units and exhaust ducts adjacent to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and blast booths; material staging areas between blasting and heat treat operations.

Lubricant specification: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-426.

Examples of affected scenarios:
- Workpiece moved from a blasting booth on P2, line P2-L4 into the staging area adjacent to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 without interim cleaning or control, resulting in visible dust transfer onto furnace load carts.
- Dust accumulation on exterior furnace doors and seals of EQ-P2-L4-HT02 leading to increased sealing wear and ingress of particulates into the furnace chamber.
- Extraction failures in booths that allow plume escape into the work environment in the vicinity of EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

## Required controls
Engineering controls
- Verify containment integrity of all blasting booths on P2, line P2-L4. Booth doors, seals, and curtain interfaces must prevent visible leakage of dust to adjacent zones.
- Confirm functioning of local exhaust ventilation for blast booths and neighboring areas; ensure duct routing prevents re-entrainment toward EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- Install or verify existing capture ventilation at the loading interface between blasting stations and the staging area that leads into EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

Administrative controls
- Implement a staging protocol for parts moving from blasting to EQ-P2-L4-HT02: parts must be placed on a designated cleaned surface and visually inspected for residual dust prior to transfer to furnace loading carts.
- Require operators to follow SOP-P2-L4-03 for pre-heat treat staging and handling on P2, line P2-L4. Deviations must be documented and routed per ECN-2026-020 when they affect process flow.
- Use line-side checklists referenced in MM-P2-L4-HT02 for furnace servicing and cleaning to ensure lubricant and maintenance actions for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 use the specified lubricant part number CFW-LUB-426 and that surface contamination risks are evaluated before furnace access.

Personal protective equipment
- Ensure blasting operators and receiving personnel wear approved respiratory protection whenever visual dust is present in the breathing zone, per site respiratory protection program. Respirator selection and fit verification are governed by site program requirements.

Housekeeping and cleaning
- Clean staging surfaces and load carts prior to placing parts destined for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Use HEPA-filtered vacuums or wet-clean methods; avoid dry sweeping that re-entrains dust.
- Maintain records of cleaning actions for staging areas and load carts as part of the records listed below.

Monitoring and response
- Conduct visual monitoring of blast booths and staging areas during operation shifts. If visible dust migration toward EQ-P2-L4-HT02 is observed, pause transfers and implement corrective actions identified in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Escalate persistent or recurring dust migration issues to maintenance using MM-P2-L4-HT02 as the maintenance reference and to process engineering per ECN-2026-020 for potential design changes.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for verifying booth containment: preventing escape at the source reduces load on downstream controls and prevents furnace contamination, preserving part quality and reducing time spent on corrective cleaning.
- Example: If blast curtain overlap is found to gap at the lower edge during visual inspection, secure temporary sealing until permanent repair via MM-P2-L4-HT02 is scheduled through the normal maintenance request flow.
- Rationale for staging inspections: small particulate loads that are not noticeable during blasting can transfer into furnace loads and plate out on furnace internals, causing hot spots or surface staining. A brief inspection step at staging is a low-effort control that prevents higher-cost corrective actions.

Records to keep
- Staging inspection logs for transfers from blasting to furnace staging. Include operator name and description of action taken if residual dust was found.
- Booth containment and ventilation check records, maintained as part of the preventative maintenance files referenced in MM-P2-L4-HT02.
- Cleaning action records for staging surfaces and loading carts, with method used (HEPA vacuum or wet-clean) and operator initials.
- Any deviations or process changes routed per ECN-2026-020 and any SOP exceptions tracked against SOP-P2-L4-03.

Roles and responsibilities
- Operators: follow SOP-P2-L4-03 and perform staging inspections and cleaning prior to furnace loading.
- Maintenance: address containment and ventilation defects using MM-P2-L4-HT02 procedures and ensure EQ-P2-L4-HT02 lubrication uses CFW-LUB-426 as specified.
- Supervisors: ensure training and checklist completion, and escalate design or persistent issues to engineering via ECN-2026-020.

## Effective date
Effective immediately.
